title: Build and Host Your Company Website on Cargo With Your Own Domain
summary: Run the company website as code: a statically exported Next.js app hosted on Cargo, served on your www domain, with every change a reviewed pull request. What the website-building cookbook deploys, how the DNS works whether or not Cargo holds it, what it costs and what it will not do.
body_markdown:
**To build and host your company website on Cargo with your own domain, declare it as a statically exported Next.js app with` defineApp` , give it your` www` hostname, and publish the DNS records with` defineDomain` (or add them at your DNS provider): Cargo builds the app on deploy and serves every page as real HTML on your domain.** The site then lives in your go-to-market repository, and every change, from a typo to a new page, is a pull request someone reviewed before it deploys.


The[website-building cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/website-building) is that setup as a worked example your coding agent adapts. This page explains what it does end to end, what it needs, what it costs and where it stops.


## Deploy it#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com


# a new project, with the cookbook in it
cargo-ai   project   init   my-site   --cookbook   website-building   &&   cd   my-site   &&   npm   install


# or, inside an existing Cargo project
cargo-ai   project   add   cookbook/website-building


```


` project add` copies the code to` infra/website-building/` and the procedure to` .claude/skills/website-building/` , so the coding agent in that repository knows how to brief, build and ship the site. A new account starts with 100 free credits and needs no card.


Then, from the project root:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   project   plan       # shows the app, the hostname and the DNS diff record by record
cargo-ai   project   deploy     # only after you have read that diff


```


If the repository is connected to Cargo, the merged pull request is the deploy and you do not run` deploy` from a laptop.


## How it works, end to end#


Three resources make the site, and nothing else is deployed:


1. **The app.**` defineApp("website", { path, domains })` points at a Next.js package in the repository. On deploy, Cargo uploads it and runs its own` build` script:` next build` with` output: "export"` and` trailingSlash: true` , moved to` dist/` . The starter ships home and about pages,` robots.txt` , a sitemap, a theme toggle and shadcn/ui on Tailwind, with the copy in one` site.json` .
2. **The hostname.**` domains: \["www.example.com"\]` attaches your` www` host on deploy. Cargo’s own` *.app.getcargo.run` URL and every preview URL answer with` X-Robots-Tag: noindex` , so your domain is the only origin search engines index.
3. **The domain, when Cargo holds its DNS.**` defineDomain("example.com", { adopt: true, dnsRecords: \[website.domainRecords\], redirectUrl: "https://www.example.com" })` publishes the records the hostname needs (the` _cargo-verify` TXT, the certificate-validation CNAME and the` www` CNAME) and forwards the apex to` www` .


Cargo serves a path from the file the export wrote for it. For` /pricing` it serves` pricing/index.html` , then` pricing.html` , then your` 404.html` with status 404, and only then the root` index.html` .` /pricing` and` /pricing/` resolve identically, and a prerendered page reaches a crawler with its own title, description and canonical in the initial HTML.


## When your DNS is somewhere else#


Most company domains keep their DNS at a registrar or provider. In that case you delete` infra/domains/website.ts` , keep` domains` on the app, deploy once (not as a draft, which attaches no hostname) and add the three records by hand:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   hosting   app   list      # the app's uuid


curl   "https://api.getcargo.io/v1/hosting/custom-domains/list?appUuid=<app-uuid>"   \
-H   "authorization: Bearer   $CARGO_API_TOKEN  "


```


` verification` holds the` _cargo-verify` TXT and the certificate-validation CNAME, and` cnameTarget` is where` www` points. Forward the apex to` https://www.<domain>` with the provider’s redirect. Cargo never writes a zone it does not hold.


## What the deploy changes in your zone#


When Cargo holds the DNS,` dnsRecords` is merged into the live zone. Records the deploy did not write, MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC included, stay where they are, so a domain your Cargo mailboxes send from can carry the website too. Two things are replaced rather than added: the` www` CNAME takes over whatever` www` pointed to, and` redirectUrl` replaces the apex forward.` cargo-ai project plan` reads the live zone and prints every` +` ,` ~` and` -` before anything changes.


The first deploy is the exception: the hostname attaches during it, so that plan cannot list the app’s records yet. If` dig +short www.<domain>` already answers, deploy in two steps (first without` website.domainRecords` , then with it), so the second plan shows the` www` change before it happens.


## What it needs#


- A Cargo workspace and` @cargo-ai/cli` with` @cargo-ai/cdk` 1.0.92 or later, and Node.js 22.18 or later.
- A domain you control, and to know who holds its DNS.
- Approved copy.` site.json` starts as` status: "draft"` , which keeps the pages` noindex` and` robots.txt` disallowing, until someone has reviewed them.


## What it costs#


An app promoted to production is 50 credits a month, per the[Cargo credits reference](https://docs.getcargo.ai/reference/credits) , and each merge is one deployment of it. Adopting a domain the workspace already owns adds no purchase. Registering a new one through Cargo charges workspace credits once and is not refundable: the plan’s` + create domain:` line is that purchase. Nothing in the cookbook runs on a schedule.


## What it will not do#


- **Run server code.** Cargo hosts static files. Route handlers, middleware, image optimization and a form that delivers live elsewhere and are called from the page.
- **Publish a draft or invented content.** No made-up customers, numbers, prices or testimonials, and nothing ships as` ready` before review.
- **Serve on the apex.** The apex cannot CNAME to an app; it forwards to` www` .
- **Go live the moment the deploy finishes.** A hostname serves nothing until its` _cargo-verify` TXT resolves, which can take minutes to hours. A pending TXT is reported as pending.
- **Take a live site off its name.** Removing a hostname from` domains` leaves it attached; detaching is a deliberate action in Cargo.


## Questions#


Yes. Cargo detects Vite, Create React App, Gatsby and Astro, and runs any app’s own` build` script. The rule is the output: a static export in` dist/` . The cookbook uses Next.js with` output: "export"` because it gives every page its own HTML and metadata.


Not when the deploy did not write them.` dnsRecords` is merged into the zone, so MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records stay. Only` www` and the apex forward are replaced, and the plan prints both before the deploy.


Both are separate cookbooks that add to this site:[inbound-qualification](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/inbound-qualification) for a demo form that qualifies and answers each request, and[visitor-identification](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/visitor-identification) for the companies that read the site without filling anything in.


Deploy it from the[website-building cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/website-building) . For dashboards, internal tools and other hosted apps, see[Cargo apps](https://www.getcargo.ai/product/apps) .
